content:
After the addition of a Presentation structure for Groups in mathlib, @Hang Lu Su commented on the possibility of refactoring the Coxeter Groups API so that it uses the Presentation interface. Both the word length and some reindexing lemmas in GroupTheory/Coxeter don't seem to use anything specific about Coxeter groups and might be moved to other parts of Mathlib (Lu already rewrote word length in Geometry/Group/WordMetric based on what was done here).

We have some beginners interested in joining this refactor and help out, so I thought of changing the definition of CoxeterSystem to something like this:

def relation (i j : ι) : FreeGroup ι := (FreeGroup.of i * FreeGroup.of j) ^ M i j

def relationsSet : Set (FreeGroup ι) := range <| uncurry M.relation

protected def Group : Type _ := PresentedGroup M.relationsSet
deriving Group

structure CoxeterSystem (M : CoxeterMatrix ι) (G : Type*) [Group G] extends Presentation G ι where
  coxeter : rel = M.relationsSet

And then fill the rest of the proofs with sorry so that we can split the work between the people that want to participate. Would this be a useful refactor? The idea is also to start a conversation here to decide how the interface should be.
Yes, now that we have a general notion of a group with a presentation by generators and relations, CoxeterSystem should use this API.

How can we implement this refactor incrementally? I'm assuming having a single PR would make it too big for a review, but I'm not sure how it should be split into smaller ones, since changing the definition of CoxeterSystem would break all the following theorems

It's hard to answer this in the abstract: but some refactors cannot be split, and then they are reviewed as a whole because that's the only way. It's good to do this incrementally (and good to think about this!), but sometimes there is no better way. (I don't have time right now to think about a possible incremental approach.)

It seems that are only five files containing CoxeterSystem. The way I would do it would be to change the definition of CoxeterSystem, and try to see what breaks. In order to mitigate the issues, you would have to keep CoxeterSystem.mulEquiv, but as a definition (which may be deprecated in the same PR or a further PR) rather than a field of the structure. This should not break too much the downstream usages of the CoxeterSystem API. For the constructions of terms in CoxeterSystem, the code would have to be adapted: temporarily, you may introduce a constructor taking the same parameters as the "old" API, and cleanup this in a follow up PR.

Thank you very much for the answers! I guess we can always work in our own fork of mathlib, and once we advance enough, we can think about how to submit it to mathlib. @Joël Riou , thank you for the suggestion, I think I understand what you mean and will definitely try this approach in order to minimize breakage.
